body_md:
[]
For $k=1$, the term $R^{(k)}_1(x)$ in Theorem \ref{Theorem Number field analogue Id 2nd paper} reduces to
\begin{align*}
R^{(1)}_1(x) &= \lim_{s\to 1}(s-1)\Omega_\mathbb{F}(s)x^{s} \\
&= \left(\frac{D}{4^{r_2}\pi^d}\right)^{\frac{1}{2}}\Gamma^{r_1}\left(\frac{1}{2}\right)x\lim_{s\to 1}(s-1)\zeta_{\mathbb{F}}(s) \\
&= \frac{\sqrt{D}x}{(2\pi)^{r_2}}H_\mathbb{F}.
\end{align*}
Substituting this expression for $R^{(1)}_1(x)$ with $k=1$ into Theorem \ref{Theorem Number field analogue Id 2nd paper} yields the desired identity in Corollary \ref{Case k=1 mt2}.

[]
                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                         
               
                                                     
                 
             
For $\mathbb{F}=\mathbb{Q}$, we have
$$
r_1=1,\quad r_2=0,\quad D=1,\quad d=1,\quad
\gamma_{\mathbb{F}}=\gamma,\quad
\mathtt{a}_{\mathbb{F},2}(n)=d(n),\quad H_{\mathbb{F}}=1.
$$
Moreover, by \eqref{Z value real} and \eqref{Bessel fn formula},
$$
\tilde{Z}_{2r_1,2r_2}\left(\frac{4^{r_2}\pi^d nx}{D}\right)
=\tilde{Z}_{2,0}(\pi nx)
=2V(\pi^2n^2x^2\mid0,0)
=4K_0(2\pi nx).
$$
Consequently, the function $\mathcal{H}_{\mathbb{F},2}(x)$ in Corollary \ref{Gen Koshliakov Formula} becomes
\begin{align*}
\mathcal{H}_{\mathbb{Q},2}(x)
&=4\sqrt{x}\sum_{n=1}^\infty d(n)K_0(2\pi nx)
+\sqrt{x}\left[2\gamma+\log\left(\frac{x}{\pi}\right)-\gamma-2\log2\right]\\
&=\sqrt{x}\left(\gamma-\log\left(\frac{4\pi}{x}\right)\right)
+4\sqrt{x}\sum_{n=1}^\infty d(n)K_0(2\pi nx).
\end{align*}
Substituting the above expression for $\mathcal{H}_{\mathbb{Q},2}(x)$ into \eqref{Extended number field RK formula} and taking $\alpha\beta=1$, we obtain
\begin{align*}
\sqrt{\alpha}\left[
\gamma-\log\left(\frac{4\pi}{\alpha}\right)
-4\sum_{n=1}^{\infty}d(n)K_0(2\pi n\alpha)
\right]&=\sqrt{\beta}\left[
\gamma-\log\left(\frac{4\pi}{\beta}\right)
-4\sum_{n=1}^{\infty}d(n)K_0(2\pi n\beta)
\right]\\
&=\frac{32}{\pi}\int_0^\infty
\frac{\Xi^2\left(\frac t2\right)}
{(1+t^2)^2}
\cos\left(\frac t2\log\alpha\right)\text{d}t.
\end{align*}
Using $\beta=1/\alpha$ and rearranging the terms, the preceding identity takes the form
\begin{align*}
\sqrt{\alpha}\left(4\sum_{n=1}^{\infty}d(n)K_0(2\pi n\alpha) - 
\frac{\gamma-\log(4\pi\alpha)}{\alpha}\right)
&=\sqrt{\beta}\left(4\sum_{n=1}^{\infty}d(n)K_0(2\pi n\beta) - \frac{\gamma-\log(4\pi\beta)}{\beta}\right)\\
&=\frac{32}{\pi}\int_0^\infty
\frac{\Xi^2\left(\frac{t}{2}\right)}
{(1+t^2)^2}
\cos\left(\frac t2\log\alpha\right)\text{d}t.
\end{align*}
This is precisely the extended Ramanujan--Koshliakov formula \eqref{Extended Koshliakov formula}.
